texts.label: text
texts.orig: The RJA-40 is an integrated brushless-motor joint actuator for collaborative robot arms, combining a BLDC motor, a two-stage planetary/harmonic drivetrain, an absolute encoder, and an onboard joint controller in a single module. It is designed for direct EtherCAT or CAN daisy-chaining across a 6- or 7-axis arm.
texts.text: The RJA-40 is an integrated brushless-motor joint actuator for collaborative robot arms, combining a BLDC motor, a two-stage planetary/harmonic drivetrain, an absolute encoder, and an onboard joint controller in a single module. It is designed for direct EtherCAT or CAN daisy-chaining across a 6- or 7-axis arm.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The absolute encoder reports output-flange position at 16-bit resolution to the joint controller, which closes a local current/velocity/position control loop at 4 kHz and exposes a CiA 402-style profile over EtherCAT or CAN to the arm's central controller.
texts.text: The absolute encoder reports output-flange position at 16-bit resolution to the joint controller, which closes a local current/velocity/position control loop at 4 kHz and exposes a CiA 402-style profile over EtherCAT or CAN to the arm's central controller.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Rev. B module does not include an integrated torque sensor at the output flange; torque is estimated from motor current, which is less accurate under high-friction or high-backlash conditions. A strain-gauge-based torque sensor is planned for Rev. C.
